title: How can we find the mean of fifty numbers quickly?
description: A question from the book asks for the mean of the first fifty natural numbers, the first fifty odd numbers and the first fifty multiples of four. The video pairs the first number with the last to add the natural numbers, then shifts and multiplies that mean for the other two lists.
teaching_notes: One idea: the odd numbers and the multiples of four are made from the natural numbers by doubling, taking one, or multiplying by four, so their means follow from the first mean. Watch for students who add fifty numbers one by one and slip, or who halve the last number and forget that the list starts at one.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 1)
video_script.why: The child can find a mean by adding and dividing, but a list of fifty numbers is too long to add one by one.
video_script.substitution: Pair the first number with the last to get the sum, then shift or multiply the mean for the other two lists.
video_script.anchor: three strips of fifty numbers: the natural numbers, the odd numbers and the multiples of four
video_script.payoff_line: The means are twenty five point five, fifty and one hundred and two

final_answer.spoken: twenty five point five, fifty and one hundred and two

never_show: 25 as the mean of the first fifty natural numbers, marked as right
maths_rules: (ii) each odd number is 2 x n - 1 for n = 1 to 50, so the mean is 2 x 25.5 - 1 = 50; check 1 + 3 + ... + 99 = 2500 and 2500 / 50 = 50
(iii) the multiples of 4 are 4 x n, so the mean is 4 x 25.5 = 102; check 4 + 8 + ... + 200 = 5100 and 5100 / 50 = 102
video_script.design: One idea: find the first mean by pairing, then shift and multiply it. The three strips stay from ground to the end of the idea part.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; three strips of numbers: 1, 2, 3 and so on to 50; 1, 3, 5 and so on to 99; 4, 8, 12 and so on to 200

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.lists: the three strips of fifty numbers slide in one under the other
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside each strip

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about three lists of fifty numbers.
<bookmark mark='lists'/>The first list has the natural numbers. The second has the odd numbers. The third has the multiples of four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we find the mean of each list without a very long addition?

beats.on_screen: the three strips and the question marks stay; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the strips stay in view

beats.on_screen: on the first strip, arcs join 1 with 50, 2 with 49 and 3 with 48; each arc is labelled 51

marks.pair: arcs join the first number with the last, the second with the one before the last, and so on
marks.same: every arc carries the same label, 51

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. The mean is the sum divided by the count.
<bookmark mark='same'/>To find the sum quickly, join the first number with the last. Every such pair has the same total.

beats.on_screen: Given: the first 50 natural numbers, the first 50 odd numbers, the first 50 multiples of 4

marks.given: the three lists are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the first fifty natural numbers, the first fifty odd numbers and the first fifty multiples of four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the mean of each list

marks.find: the thing to find is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the mean of each list.

marks.pair: 1 + 50 = 51 is written, with 25 pairs counted on the first strip

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>Step one, the sum of the natural numbers. One plus fifty is fifty one, and fifty numbers make twenty five pairs.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Twenty five multiplied by fifty one is one thousand two hundred and seventy five.

marks.divide: 1275 ÷ 50 = 25.5 is written beside the first strip

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step two, the mean. The sum is one thousand two hundred and seventy five, and the count is fifty. Dividing gives twenty five point five.

marks.odd: each odd number is written as two times a natural number, minus one
marks.mean: 2 × 25.5 − 1 = 50 is written beside the second strip

narration: <bookmark mark='odd'/>Step three, the odd numbers. Each odd number is two times a natural number, take away one.
<bookmark mark='mean'/>Doubling the mean gives fifty one, and taking away one gives fifty.

marks.four: each multiple of four is written as four times a natural number
marks.mean: 4 × 25.5 = 102 is written beside the third strip

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, the multiples of four. Each one is four times a natural number.
<bookmark mark='mean'/>The mean is four times twenty five point five, which is one hundred and two.

marks.check: each strip gets its first and last numbers circled, and the half of their total is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check. Add the first and the last number of each list, then halve the total. This gives the same three means.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The means are twenty five point five, fifty and one hundred and two.
For evenly spaced numbers, the mean is halfway between the first and the last.
